quick.summary: Why a metric changed twice in a month, and how one owner stops it.
quick.takeaway: One owner per metric. Changes go through them.

beats.line: Two people changed the churn definition last month. Which one is right?
An owner is the one person who agrees any change.
Changes go to them, with a reason.
And the dashboard notes the date the rule changed.
Isn’t that a lot of process for one number?
One person and one note. Cheaper than two churn numbers.
I asked who owns churn. Product does. I sent my change to them.
Now everyone counts churn the same way.

quiz.question: You want to change how a metric is calculated. What should you do?
options: Send the change to the metric’s owner with a reason
Change it quietly on your dashboard
Create a second version with the same name
quiz.explanation: One owner keeps a single definition and makes sure everyone knows when it changes.

quiz.question: Anyone on the team should be able to change a shared metric definition directly.
quiz.explanation: Without one owner, definitions drift and teams end up with different numbers under the same name.
